definition: a man of high rank who holds power or authority over others
hook: A lord was not the man with the sword. He was the man in charge of the bread.
modernAnchor: A title on a letter, a robe in a chamber, a hand that grants or refuses. We call him a lord.
journey: Old English hlaf was a loaf of bread, and weard was a guard. The head of a household was its hlafweard, the loaf guardian.
His power was simple. He held the grain, so he decided who ate. The people who depended on him were called loaf eaters.
His wife had her own title, the loaf kneader. Worn down over the centuries, that one became the word lady.
Hlafweard shrank to hlaford, then to lord. The bread fell out of the word, and only the power over the hungry stayed behind.
